questions.stem: A kettle heats water using an electrical supply. Which energy transfer pathway is primarily involved?

options.text: Mechanically (by forces)
By radiation
By heating
Electrically

questions.explanation: The kettle uses electrical work to transfer energy from the mains supply to the heating element. The element then transfers energy to the water by heating. However, the primary transfer pathway from the supply to the kettle is electrical. Mechanical transfer involves forces causing movement, and radiation involves electromagnetic waves.

questions.stem: When a person pushes a box across a rough floor, energy is transferred from the chemical energy store of the person to which stores?

options.text: Only the kinetic energy store of the box
The kinetic energy store of the box and the thermal energy store of the floor and box
Only the thermal energy store of the floor
The gravitational potential energy store of the box

questions.explanation: When the box moves, it gains kinetic energy. Friction between the box and the rough floor also transfers energy to the thermal energy stores of both surfaces, warming them up. The gravitational potential energy does not change because the box stays on the same level. Energy is transferred both usefully (kinetic) and wastefully (thermal).

questions.stem: The Sun warms the Earth's surface. By which pathway is this energy transferred?

options.text: By heating through conduction
By heating through convection
By radiation (electromagnetic waves)
Mechanically

questions.explanation: Energy from the Sun travels to Earth by radiation in the form of electromagnetic waves (mainly infrared, visible light, and ultraviolet). Conduction and convection both require particles, and space is a vacuum with almost no particles. Mechanical transfer requires a force moving an object.

questions.stem: A car brakes and comes to a stop. What happens to the kinetic energy store of the car?

options.text: It is destroyed
It is transferred to the gravitational potential energy store
It is transferred to the thermal energy stores of the brakes and surroundings
It is transferred to the chemical energy store of the fuel

questions.explanation: When brakes are applied, friction forces between the brake pads and discs convert kinetic energy into thermal energy, heating the brakes and surrounding air. Energy cannot be destroyed (conservation of energy), so option A is wrong. The energy does not return to the fuel's chemical store or convert to gravitational potential energy on a flat road.

questions.stem: A wind turbine generates electricity. Which sequence correctly describes the energy transfer pathway?

options.text: Chemical store of wind -> electrical transfer -> thermal store in homes
Kinetic store of wind -> mechanical transfer -> electrical transfer -> energy in homes
Nuclear store of wind -> kinetic store of turbine -> electrical transfer
Gravitational store of air -> kinetic store of turbine -> light

questions.explanation: Wind has kinetic energy due to moving air particles. This kinetic energy is transferred mechanically to the turbine blades, which spin a generator. The generator then transfers energy electrically to homes. Wind does not have chemical or nuclear energy stores. The energy originates from the Sun heating the atmosphere unevenly.
